name: Learn visible mending
blurb: Sashiko-style repair that treats the mend as decoration rather than something to hide. It is easier than invisible mending and looks deliberate rather than shabby.
gear: Sashiko or embroidery thread in a contrasting colour
Patch fabric, often denim or cotton
A long needle and a thimble
steps: Assess the damage and cut a patch that extends well beyond the worn area into sound fabric.
Pin or baste the patch behind the hole, or on top for a bolder look.
Stitch rows of even running stitch across the whole patch area in a grid or wave pattern.
Keep the stitches and the gaps consistent — the rhythm is the aesthetic.
Work outward from the damage so the stress spreads across a wide area rather than at the hole edge.
tips: Anchoring only at the hole edge concentrates strain and it tears again next to your work.
Contrast thread is the point. Half-hearted matching thread looks like a mistake instead of a choice.
proof: A mended garment you would wear out of the house and be pleased to have someone notice.
